Select context tree settings by cross-validated perplexity

Source: R/tune.R
tune_tree.Rd

tune_tree() selects the settings of a variable-order context tree by cross-validated perplexity. Four settings decide how much history the tree uses and how far it trusts sparse histories: the maximum depth, the minimum count a context needs to be kept, the smoothing of the next-state distributions, and whether the tree is pruned. A deeper, less smoothed tree reproduces the sequences it was fitted to more closely, but it does not necessarily predict new sequences better. Held-out perplexity measures the second property: it is the exponential of the mean negative log-likelihood per scored transition in sequences the model has not seen, and can be read as the effective number of next states the model is choosing between.

It fits a tree for every combination of the supplied values and scores it by k-fold cross-validation. Folds are formed from whole sequences, so a held-out sequence contributes no transitions to the fit, and every configuration is scored on the same folds. The selected configuration is the one with the lowest held-out perplexity among those that scored on every fold; a configuration with a failed fold is kept in the grid but is never selected. It returns the grid as a transitiontrees_tune data frame with one row per configuration, lowest held-out perplexity first.

The grid compares settings by out-of-sample prediction. To describe the fit of one tree to its own data use model_fit() or perplexity(); to compare smoothing methods or pruning rules on one data set without cross-validation use compare_smoothing() and compare_pruning().

Usage

tune_tree(
  data,
  max_depth = 2L:5L,
  min_count = c(3L, 5L, 10L),
  smoothing = "floor",
  prune = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  alpha = 0.05,
  folds = 5L,
  seed = 1L,
  actor = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  time_threshold = 900
)

Arguments

data

Sequences in any format accepted by context_tree().

max_depth

Maximum depths to try. Default 2:5.

min_count

Minimum context counts to try. Default c(3, 5, 10).

smoothing

Smoothing methods to try: a character vector of method names, each used with its default settings (default "floor"), or a list of specifications such as list(list("floor", ymin = 0.001), list("floor", ymin = 0.005)) to vary the settings of one method.

prune

Whether to prune with the \(G^2\) criterion; both values are tried by default (c(FALSE, TRUE)).

alpha

Significance level of the \(G^2\) pruning test. Default 0.05.

folds

Number of cross-validation folds. Default 5.

seed

Seed for the assignment of sequences to folds. Default 1. The call sets the session's random-number state.

actor, time, action, order, session, time_threshold

Column names and session gap for a long event log, as in context_tree(); the log is reshaped with prepare_input() before tuning. Default NULL (data already one row per sequence) and 900 seconds.

Value

An object of class transitiontrees_tune: a data frame with one row per configuration, sorted by held-out perplexity (lowest first), and columns max_depth, min_count, smoothing, prune, logLik (held-out log-likelihood summed over the folds that scored; NA when none did), n_scored (held-out transitions scored), perplexity, n_nodes_avg (mean number of contexts of the fitted trees) and folds_failed (folds that could not be fitted or scored). as.data.frame(x, what = "best") returns the selected configuration, summary() a one-row overview, and plot() the perplexity surface.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) fewer sequences than folds; smoothing neither a character vector nor a list; data not in a sequence format.

transitiontrees_fold_failed

(warning) at least one configuration had a fold that could not be fitted or scored; the message gives the first error.

transitiontrees_no_best

(warning) no configuration scored on every fold, so none is selected.

See also

summary.transitiontrees_tune, as.data.frame.transitiontrees_tune and plot.transitiontrees_tune for the result; context_tree() and prune_tree() to fit the selected configuration; perplexity() and model_fit() for the fit of one tree.

Examples

tuned <- tune_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 1:3, min_count = c(5, 10),
                   prune = c(FALSE, TRUE), folds = 3)
tuned
#> <transitiontrees_tune>  12 configurations
